title: INT8 weight-only: cross-model calibration matrix and nightly regression harness
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Goal: Build an automated integration and nightly regression pipeline that validates INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ and AWQ) across a representative cross-model calibration matrix. This ticket covers: 1) assembling calibration datasets (per-model calibration shards, activation histograms, per-layer statistics), 2) implementing pipeline steps to run GPTQ and AWQ passes with fixed seeds and output profiles, 3) automated accuracy evaluation against golden prompts/evals and QoE thresholds, 4) fail/rollback policies and dashboarding for regressions. Scope excludes live user traffic experiments and on-prem packaging (handled in separate Private deployment tickets).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Nightly job runs end-to-end for target model set (Llama-2-13B, Red-Base-7B, Mixtral-8x7B) producing profile artifacts and eval metrics; 2) Regression detector flags model-profile pairs that exceed top-level QoE thresholds (perplexity/regression delta) and creates a Linear incident; 3) Ability to replay any nightly run locally with a deterministic seed; 4) Profiles are versioned and stored in S3 with metadata (model, seed, quant-lib, commit); 5) Run-time fallback: if a profile fails validation, serving routes default to FP16 variant per rollout policy.
test_matrix: Models: mix of small/med/large open models (3-13B). Calibration shards: 5 distinct shards per model (domain: conversational, docs, code, search). Sequence lengths: 64, 256, 1024. Quant libs: GPTQ v1.2 (channel-wise), AWQ v0.9 (per-tensor), and baseline naive p8 emulation. Metrics: token perplexity, BLEU for structured outputs, embedding cosine drift, and decode-time latency. Acceptance thresholds: perplexity <= baseline+3%, BLEU >= baseline-2 pts, embedding drift <= 0.02 cosine, latency overhead <= 1.15x.
progress: Prototype pipeline implemented as airflow DAG and a lightweight runner for local replay. GPTQ and AWQ tuning knobs exposed via CLI. Initial run completed for Red-Base-7B on 2026-02-12; observed a 2.8% perplexity increase vs FP16 for one shard, within threshold. Next: broaden model set and stabilize seed handling.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: non-determinism in GPU kernels causing noisy eval signals. Mitigation: enforce fixed RNG seeds, CPU ref runs for delta sanity, and record kernel/binary versions. Risk: calibration dataset skew leading to false regressions. Mitigation: stratified sampling in shards and weight on cross-shard median metrics.
rollout_plan: 1) Run nightly for a 3-model canary set for two weeks; 2) Add automated regression alerting to Slack + create incident with triage checklist when thresholds breach; 3) Promote validated profiles to dedicated-serving train (for Dedicated customers) and publish profile metadata in model-catalog with compatibility tags.
observability_and_dashboarding: Create Grafana dashboard with per-model/per-profile time series: perplexity, BLEU, embedding-drift, quantization-error histogram, and job success rate. Add links in dashboard to S3 artifacts and GitHub PRs for the run. Alerting: severity P1 if any model-profile shows >5% perplexity regression sustained for 3 consecutive nights.
automation_notes: Nightly CI uses a separate k8s nodepool with GPU taints. Jobs executed under docker image registry.redwood/quant-harness:2026-03-10. Store artifacts in s3://redwood-quant-profiles/nightly/<date>/<model>/<profile>. Profiles include meta.json with seed/commit/quant-lib.

implementation_notes:
- Use same quant-lib versions across nightly jobs and record them in meta.json.
- Persist raw logits and decoded outputs for golden evals for debug.
- Implement profile signing to prevent accidental serving with mismatched profiles.
- Keep a compact index of profile compatibility in model-catalog service for fast lookup by runtime.
